global.title: Iran conflict widens as strikes hit Kuwait and regional tensions spread
global.summary: Iran said it struck U.S. assets in Kuwait after U.S. strikes inside Iran, signaling a dangerous new phase in the conflict and raising fears of broader regional escalation.
global.whyItMatters: This shapes prayer, preaching, and pastoral care as many in the church feel anxiety over war, peace, and global stability.

global.title: Qatari-mediated proposal may reopen Strait of Hormuz
global.summary: A new proposal reportedly received a positive response from Iranian diplomats and could reopen shipping through the Strait of Hormuz under a revised transit arrangement.
global.whyItMatters: Any movement toward de-escalation affects global markets, public anxiety, and opportunities to speak about peacemaking and wise leadership.

global.title: Ceuta migrant crisis deepens with mass crossings and rising death toll
global.summary: Spanish authorities are tightening border measures after tens of thousands entered Ceuta, with dozens reported dead and many migrants, including children, left without shelter.
global.whyItMatters: This is a vivid reminder of the human cost of displacement and a call for prayerful attention to refugees, mercy, and justice.

canadian.title: Canadian tourism to the U.S. fell sharply amid political tensions
canadian.summary: New data show Canadians made 7.1 million fewer trips to the U.S. in 2025, while domestic and overseas travel increased instead.
canadian.whyItMatters: This reflects shifting public mood and economic pressure, offering insight into the concerns and conversations people may be carrying into church life.

canadian.title: WestJet strike threat disrupts long-weekend travel plans
canadian.summary: More than 300 flights have been cancelled as flight attendants and WestJet remain far apart in negotiations over pay and unpaid work time.
canadian.whyItMatters: Travel disruption affects families, stress levels, and pastoral rhythms, especially during summer when many in the congregation are away or hosting visitors.

local.title: HandyDART app rollout coming to Abbotsford, Mission, and Chilliwack
local.summary: BC Transit is introducing a new app for HandyDART riders to book, manage, and track trips, while keeping phone booking available.
local.whyItMatters: Improved accessibility matters pastorally for seniors and people with disabilities, and may help churches think more clearly about inclusion and transportation barriers.

local.title: Highway 1 remains closed near Boston Bar as wildfire situation continues
local.summary: The Brunswick Complex fires are not growing significantly at present, but both major fires remain out of control and Highway 1 stays closed between Spuzzum Creek Road and Jackass Summit.
local.whyItMatters: This continues to affect travel, safety, and community stress across the Fraser Valley, making it a live pastoral concern for prayer and care.

local.title: Cultus Lake Waterpark reopens after electrical incident review
local.summary: The waterpark has reopened with reduced operations after a six-week closure following the incident that injured schoolchildren, with safety reviews still shaping what areas can operate.
local.whyItMatters: Local families will notice this development, and it speaks to community recovery, public trust, and care for those still affected.

persecutedChurch.title: U.S. condemns killing of Nigerian pastor’s relatives
persecutedChurch.summary: The U.S. has denounced the killing of nine relatives of Pastor Ezekiel Dachomo and called for stronger protection of Christians in Nigeria’s violence-hit Middle Belt.
persecutedChurch.whyItMatters: This is a clear call to pray for the suffering church and to remember believers facing deadly pressure for their faith.

persecutedChurch.title: Thirty-five Christians killed in eastern Congo
persecutedChurch.summary: Barnabas Aid reports that 35 Christians were killed by Islamists in Ituri Province, adding to ongoing trauma for churches already living under severe instability.
persecutedChurch.whyItMatters: It helps keep global intercession grounded in real people, real churches, and urgent need for comfort, justice, and endurance.

leadership.title: 7 leadership actions to strengthen talent sustainability
leadership.summary: Forbes highlights practical leadership habits such as developing people internally, building continuous learning, and designing for whole-life careers rather than short-term staffing fixes.
leadership.whyItMatters: For a pastor leading staff and volunteers, this offers a useful framework for building a healthier, more durable ministry culture.

goodNews.title: Global hunger falls below 8% for the first time since the pandemic
goodNews.summary: A new FAO-referenced report says global hunger has dropped to 7.8%, an encouraging milestone even as conflict remains a major driver of need.
goodNews.whyItMatters: This is a hopeful reminder that progress is possible and can encourage gratitude, prayer, and renewed commitment to mercy ministries.
